prerequisites: Knowledge of manufacturing processes and the most commonly used production systems in the modern manufacturing industry.
Basic knowledge of micro and macro economics.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire advanced knowledge of all the necessary activities required to plan and control manufacturing production.
Integrate knowledge gained in technologies and manufacturing systems, industrial equipment and industrial logistics to form insights.
Enrich the understanding of the main management policies of production and for production planning tools in the medium/long term.
Acquire a clear awareness of the wider multidisciplinary context of engineering.

syllabus_topics: GENERAL ASPECTS OF MANUFACTURING. Role and evolution of manufacturing, technical and management functions, planning and production control, decision-making process.
DEMAND MANAGEMENT. General aspects, techniques of demand forecasting, qualitative methods, quantitative methods (causal and time series models), and application cases.

INDEPENDENT DEMAND MATERIAL MANAGEMENT. The role of the stocks, stock accounting systems, classification methods, inventory costs, and models for management of continuous and independent demand materials (fixed order quantity and fixed order interval models).
AGGREGATE PRODUCTION PLANNING. Fundamental aspects, aims, aggregate production planning process, quantitative models, disaggregation, and application cases.
MASTER PRODUCTION SCHEDULING. Definitions, ATP stocks calculation, review of MPS, and application cases.
MATERIAL REQUIREMENT PLANNING. MRP systems, input/output of MRP, processing of MRP plans, MRP update, uncertainty management in MRP, lot sizing, nervousness of MRP systems, and application cases.
CAPACITY PLANNING. General aspects, techniques of capacity planning, input/output control, and application cases.
assessment_rules: The final exam is a written test on theoretical topics and practical exercises. Two interim written assessment tests are conducted during the semester; passing these with at least 18/30 exempts the student from the full exam. The evaluation considers basic knowledge, clarity, formal and conceptual correctness, and accuracy of calculations and assumptions. The grade is expressed in thirtieths, with 18/30 for elementary knowledge and 30/30 (with possible honors) for excellent knowledge. An oral examination may supplement the written exam.
